name: bridge-tally
description: Ask about the TallyPrime books on this computer, and prepare Journal, Payment, Receipt and Contra vouchers as a local file. Posting is off until you turn it on below; then it posts one voucher at a time, each after you approve it in a native dialog. What it reads, amounts included, goes to your AI provider; Response redaction can only mask party names or drop narration.

accept_terms_2026_10.title: I accept the ComplyEaze Bridge Terms of Use (version 2026-10)
accept_terms_2026_10.description: Required: ComplyEaze Bridge refuses every tool call until you accept. Terms: https://bridge.complyeaze.com/terms. Privacy: https://bridge.complyeaze.com/privacy.

host.title: Tally host
host.description: Where Tally runs on this computer: localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1.

port.title: Tally port
port.description: Tally's HTTP port on this computer.

redaction.title: Response redaction
redaction.description: What to hide from your AI provider: none, mask_parties (masks party names) or drop_narration (removes narration). Neither hides amounts. Any other value stops the connector from starting.

enable_writes.title: Allow voucher posting (Journal, Payment, Receipt, Contra)
enable_writes.description: Off by default. When on, ComplyEaze Bridge can post one Journal, Payment, Receipt or Contra into Tally at a time, each only after you approve it in a native dialog. Leave it off unless you accept three known limits. 1) Tally picks the company by name. ComplyEaze Bridge checks just before the post that exactly one open company has the target's GUID and name and no other has the same name ignoring case and spacing (bridge#607), but a company renamed to, or opened under, that name (or one differing only in case or spacing) right after the check could still receive the voucher. It may flag this afterwards, but cannot always say where the voucher went, and cannot prevent it (bridge#574). 2) A ledger renamed and replaced in that same moment can receive the post instead. This is marked for reconciliation when seen, but not every such change is seen (bridge#623). 3) There is no undo: a wrong post must be corrected by hand in Tally (bridge#579). This setting also lets you record, in a separate native dialog, that you reviewed a posted voucher whose ledgers changed master; that writes nothing to Tally. Reading, bank-statement parsing and voucher file preparation work either way.
